definition_quote.value: "Practice of environmental health" means the use of public health principles in the application of the sanitary sciences to prevent human injury and illness by: 1. Identifying and evaluating hazardous physical, chemical and biological agents that may adversely affect human health and the environmental sources of those agents; and 2. Limiting exposures to those agents in air, water, soil, food and other environmental media or settings.

Employees of the Cannabis Compliance Board conducting cannabis compliance inspections (unless cannabis is used in food products)
Consultants certified by the State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources performing hazardous waste cleanup and disposal (unless performed directly for a public health agency)
Industrial hygienists, public educators, indoor air quality specialists, health physicists, mold assessors, and mold remediators
Zoonotic disease ecology or vector-borne disease ecology specialists when practiced as a specialty
Mining employees or contractors of a mining company engaged in mining operations in the State
Building inspectors whose primary purpose is to determine compliance with building and safety codes
Epidemiologists or disease investigators performing epidemiological investigations

Persons practicing environmental health on a limited basis (not more than 45 days per year) who hold a valid unrestricted credential from another U.S. jurisdiction with substantially similar requirements
